Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

disappear verb

also vanish, disappear from sight, fade away, go missing, be nowhere to be seen

classical

Verg. A. 9.658: ex oculīs ēvānuit (Lewis & Short)
Cic. de Or. 2.95: omnis eōrum memoria sēnsim obscūrāta est et ēvānuit (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 304

ēvānēscō, ēvānēscere, ēvānuī

verb, third conjugation, intransitive

vanish, fade away, die away

Of things that fade until they are gone: a sound, a colour, a hope, a memory, a custom; with ex oculīs, of something seen. Lewis & Short also has it of wine that loses its strength with age (Cic. Div. 2.57).

Other words

  • ē cōnspectū abīre — go out of sight

    phrase; also sē ē cōnspectū auferre · also used · classical · Phaedr. App. 28.7–10: sēque ē cōnspectū abstulit; Traupman 96, 304: ē cōnspectū auferrī

    Of a person or an animal that goes off and is lost to view.

  • nusquam appāreō, appārēre — be nowhere to be seen

    phrase: nusquam with appāreō, verb, second conjugation · also used · classical · Ter. Eun. 4.3.18: ille bonus vir nusquam adparet (Lewis & Short)

    The way to say that something is missing (keys, a shoe, a person): Latin says it appears nowhere.

Examples

  • et procul in tenuem ex oculīs ēvānuit auram

    and far off he vanished from sight into thin airVerg. A. 9.658 (Lewis & Short)

  • vērum haec jam etiam inter ipsās ineptiās ēvānuērunt

    but these (spellings) have now disappeared even among the folliesQuint. 1.7.6

  • vēnātor citus nōn intellēxit sēque ē cōnspectū abstulit

    the hunter in his haste did not understand, and took himself off out of sightPhaedr. App. 28.7–10

  • ille bonus vir nusquam adparet

    that fine fellow is nowhere to be seenTer. Eun. 4.3.18 (Lewis & Short)

  • Clāvēs meae nusquam appārent.

    My keys have disappeared.composed

See also get lost, go, lose.
